experiments.title: Flight-computer PCB
experiments.summary: A KiCad board for a 38 mm airframe: Pico, BMP390, ±32 g IMU, microSD. Kalman filter + state machine firmware, tested on synthetic flights.
experiments.safety: Data logger only: no pyro outputs. Certified motors, club launches.

experiments.title: LoRa telemetry ground station
experiments.summary: 915 MHz LoRa downlink with a 34-byte CRC-checked frame, a real link budget, and a Python ground station with live plots, map and a simulated flight mode.
experiments.safety: Transmit only within FCC Part 15.247 limits, or under Part 97 with a licence.

experiments.title: Barn-door star tracker
experiments.summary: Two boards, an M6 rod and a 28BYJ-48 cancel Earth's rotation. Tangent-corrected sidereal firmware keeps the error under 0.25 arcsec for an hour.

experiments.title: High-power certification
experiments.summary: The NAR / Tripoli Level 1 → 2 → 3 path: what each allows, the certification flight, FAA Part 101, NFPA 1127, insurance, clubs and costs — researched and cited.
experiments.safety: Commercially certified motors only, at sanctioned launches with an RSO.

experiments.title: OpenRocket deep dive
experiments.summary: Drive OpenRocket properly, then build 1-, 2- and 3-DOF Python simulators, verify them against closed-form physics and fit Cd to a logged flight.

experiments.title: Near-space balloon CubeSat
experiments.summary: A printed 1U CubeSat-format payload flown to ~26 km on a weather balloon: mass, power and thermal budgets, APRS tracking, landing prediction, FAA Part 101.
experiments.safety: Stay Part 101-exempt by design; APRS needs an amateur licence.

experiments.title: Hydrogen-line radio telescope
experiments.summary: A 17 dBi foam-board horn designed from first principles, an LNA and an RTL-SDR: measure 21 cm Doppler shifts and the Milky Way's flat rotation curve.

experiments.title: Exoplanet transit photometry
experiments.summary: Catch a hot Jupiter dimming its star by 2 %: a full aperture-photometry and transit-fit pipeline, proven on a synthetic night, ready for NASA Exoplanet Watch.
